folder_html:
LIVE ATMOSPHERIC VISIBILITY

Near-surface meteorological visibility from the operational HRRR analysis: how far a human observer, mariner, or pilot can distinguish surroundings through haze, mist, precipitation, and smoke. Low values flag navigation and shoreline hazards; high values mark crystal-clear Great Lakes air.

Visibility science (atmospheric optics and observing practice) quantifies horizontal contrast loss from scattering and absorption by hydrometeors and aerosols. It underpins aviation flight rules, marine navigation advisories, and air-quality perception, and is reported operationally in statute miles across the United States.


Meteorological visibility in statute miles (HRRR surface analysis, fixed absolute scale): LOWEST 0 Obscured maroon → very poor → poor → moderate yellow → good green → very good cyan → blue → HIGHEST+ 30 Crystal clear deep blue. The key steps evenly (0/5/10/15/20/25/30) with observing quality written under each value. Same visibility always shows the same color; above 30 mi clamps into deep blue. Human-observer/mariner/pilot visibility through haze, mist, precipitation, and smoke — not astronomical seeing.
Units: mi, statute (display; source m / 1609.344)
